items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's first choice for Black is 23...Re7.

hints: Ask which pawn move Black might want soon, and which pieces stand in its way.
Both black rooks are on the back rank and the f-pawn has not moved. Which rook could change files and stay useful?
A rook goes to the seventh rank on the e-file.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine puts 23...Re7 first. It is the game move. This is evidence for one position at one depth, not proof that it is the only good move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine puts the game move 31...g5 first, with 31...h5 within 40 centipawns of it.

hints: Black's kingside pawns are still on g6 and h7. Ask which advance would open a file or diagonal for Black's pieces.
Two pawn advances are close in the engine's ranking.
One of them is the game move; the other pushes a different pawn.
items.explain: At depth 16 the engine puts the game move 31...g5 first and 31...h5 close behind: both are within 40 centipawns of the best, so both are accepted here. Kasparov played 31...g5. Evidence at one depth, not proof.
